history.summary: NOT A HINDU TEMPLE — keep-or-drop decision needed (Buddhist monastery). A Nyingma gompa overlooking the confluence of the Lachen and Lachung rivers at ~2,750–3,000 m; founding-date conflict — Wikipedia and most sources give 1880, while the Sikkim Ecclesiastical Affairs Dept. records Lachung 'Samten Choling' built in the iron-dog year of the XIVth Rabjung cycle, i.e. 1850, and notes it was previously a Bon site converted by locals (verify). Copper statues of Buddha, Guru and Chenrezig plus Kangyur and Tengyur texts were brought from Tibet in 1930; renovated and remodelled by lamas in 1983. The Dukhang (assembly hall) carries murals of Buddhist mythology and gurus. Lachung was a pre-1950 India–Tibet trading post; permits are required for North Sikkim visits.

name: Lachung Monastery
town_description: Lachung ('small mountain') is a high valley town in North Sikkim at about 3,000 m, the last inhabited settlement before the Indo-Tibetan border and the gateway to Yumthang Valley; its winter mask-dance festival is famous and North Sikkim entry permits are required.

travel.road: ~118 km north of Gangtok on the North Sikkim Highway; only by road (shared/private vehicles), typically via Gangtok with a permit

visitor_information.best_time: March to June and October to December; snow access may block winter roads
visitor_information.opening_hours: Daytime hours; one listing advises visiting before 16:00 — verify locally
